raw_response:
I am 72 years old this year, and I have been working this land for 50 years. I only finished primary school, but I know every piece of my 9 mu farm. My son works in a factory in town, so it is just me and my wife doing the farming now. We have 7 mu where we do wheat-maize double cropping, and 2 mu of cotton on the side. I do what I have always done, and I watch what my neighbors do.

For wheat on the 7 mu, I rotary till the field before sowing in October. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base — that is 50 kg of 15-21-6 compound. When the wheat starts jointing in March or April, I topdress another half bag per mu. I irrigate 4 times: at sowing, at wintering, at jointing, and at grain filling. Pumping water costs money, but 4 times is what everyone around here does, and I am not going to risk the crop going dry. I spray herbicide twice and insecticide once if I see aphids. I use Jimai 22, which is an improved variety my neighbor gave me seeds from years ago. Last year I got 1000 jin per mu, so I expect about 500 kg per mu again.

For summer maize, as soon as the wheat comes off in June, I sow Denghai 605 directly into the stubble with no tillage — there is no time to plough, the season is too tight. I put down 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, that is 40 kg of 26-8-8. I irrigate twice, once at sowing and once at the big trumpet stage if the rain does not come. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once for the corn borer. Last year I got 1000 jin per mu, so 500 kg per mu is what I expect.

For cotton on my 2 mu, I rotary till in April. I use 80 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu, that is 40 kg. Cotton needs more spraying than grain — I spray insecticide 4 times and herbicide once because the weeds and bugs are bad. I irrigate twice. Last year I got 700 jin per mu, which is 350 kg. I keep it to 2 mu because picking cotton is hard work, and with my son away, me and my wife cannot handle more.

Fertilizer is expensive now, every bag is real money. But I would rather put a bit more than lose yield. A bad harvest is a disaster for my family. My neighbor down the road, who is about my age and has a similar farm, did about the same last year and had a good result. So I will do the same.
